output: {"answers":{"d05":"检测阳性就等于得病吗？贝叶斯公式回答的正是这个问题：已知 P(阳|病)(病人被检出阳性的比例)，如何倒推 P(病|阳)(阳性者真患病的概率)。设想10000人体检，患病率1%:100人患病、9900人健康。灵敏度99%——99个病人呈阳性；假阳性率5%——约495个健康人也呈阳性。于是594个阳性里只有99个真患病，P(病|阳)=99÷594≈17%。公式 P(病|阳)=P(阳|病)×P(病)÷P(阳),含义就是「真阳性占全部阳性的比例」。患病率这个先验起的作用大得违反直觉：换成高发人群(患病率10%),同样准确的检测，阳性可信度跳到约67%(990÷1485)。所以收到阳性结果，先问基础比例，再看检测精度——这就是用数据更新信念的贝叶斯思路。","d03":"麦克风靠音箱太近，轻微杂音被拾进话筒、放大后播出，又被话筒拾到——每绕一圈都同向增强，几秒内变成刺耳啸叫。这就是正反馈：输出回授到输入并与原变化同向，微小偏差一轮轮放大。判断依据是「结果是否加强原因的方向」，与好坏无关。冰雪融化后地表吸热更多、融化更快，是物理中的正反馈；银行挤兑「见人取钱→我也去取」，是坏的正反馈。「正」只指放大，不指好事，评价要看放大的是什么。放大还需增益大于1,否则波动自行衰减；现实中总有饱和——功率上限、可融冰量——所以系统最终停在极限而非无限膨胀。与之对照，负反馈抵消偏差，才有恒温器式的稳定。迁移：社交媒体上转发越多越被推荐，看到「结果反过来助长原因」，就应预期剧烈放大而非平稳。","v08":"Little's law answers a simple question: how many items are inside a system on average? In steady state, L = λW — average number in the system equals arrival rate times average time each item spends there. Coffee shop: 10 customers arrive per hour, each stays about half an hour, so on average 5 people are inside. The logic: each arrival occupies the system for duration W, so occupancy builds at rate λ; in steady state (arrivals = departures, long-run averages), stock = flow × time. Note what it does not claim: it holds for any queue discipline, FIFO or LIFO, as long as the system is stable. Change one condition: if each customer stays a full hour instead, average occupancy doubles to 10. Transfer to computing: a server handling 100 requests/second with 0.2 s average latency must have about 20 requests in flight. It is a capacity check, not a performance fix.","v03":"长颈鹿的脖子常被讲成「越伸越长」练出来的，这恰是要避开的误解。自然选择不需要任何个体主动努力：种群里本就有随机变异——有的脖子天生稍长，变异的产生是随机的；而脖子稍长的个体吃到更多树叶、活得更久、留下更多后代，筛选的方向不随机。结果不是某个动物变高了，而是种群中「长脖基因」的比例一代代升高——进化改变的是种群的比例构成，个体的身体一生不变。条件一变，判断随之变：若树叶充足，脖长差异不影响繁殖，选择压力消失；干旱使低处叶子枯死，差异才被放大。迁移：抗生素耐药不是细菌「练出」了抗药，而是用药后，碰巧耐药的少数个体存活并繁殖，后代全是耐药者。记住判断标准：变异先于选择、随机产生、非随机保留。","v06":"Deadlock is a permanent standoff: each party holds a resource and waits for one the other holds, so nobody ever moves. Picture two bank transfers: thread A locks account 1, then needs account 2; meanwhile thread B locks account 2, then needs account 1. A waits for B to release account 2; B waits for A to release account 1. Neither releases anything while waiting, so both block forever and the money stays frozen. Four conditions must all hold: exclusive resources, holding one while requesting another, no forcible taking, and a circular wait — break any one and deadlock becomes impossible. Easiest fix: a global lock order — everyone locks account 1 before account 2. Then B grabs account 1 first, A waits, B finishes and releases, and A proceeds; the circle becomes a line. The same pattern appears in databases when two transactions lock rows in opposite orders — the cure is ordering or timeouts, not hope.","v05":"信息熵衡量「平均而言你有多难预测结果」。公式 H=−Σp·log₂p:把每种结果的概率乘以它的对数再求和取负。为什么均匀分布通常更不确定？对比两枚硬币：均匀硬币正反各50%,你毫无偏向、猜中把握最小，H=1比特；做了手脚的硬币正面99%,你几乎每次都猜正面、极少惊讶，H≈0.08比特。概率越集中，不确定性越低；完全均匀时达到最大，因为你被剥夺了一切偏向。取对数是为了让信息量可加：两次独立抛掷的概率相乘，而意外程度应相加，log 正好把乘变加。条件变化：硬币从50:50偏向90:10,熵随之下降——分布每偏离均匀一点，确定性就多一点。迁移：数据熵越高越难压缩；密码越随机(熵越大)越难猜。","v01":"想象一个学生背下了所有练习题的答案，模拟考满分，一换新题就不会——这就是过拟合。机器学习模型本该从训练数据中学规律，但模型太灵活或训练太久时，它会把数据里的细节和噪音也当成规律记下来。判断依据：训练数据上表现极好，换到没见过的新数据上明显变差——记住了「答案」而非「方法」。条件变化：给它更多数据，噪音互相抵消，死记不再划算；把模型改简单，它被迫只学大趋势——但删过头连真规律也学不到，叫欠拟合。实用做法是留一批没参与训练的「验证数据」当新题，随时检查模型是真学会还是在背。迁移到生活：理财建议若按过去每波行情的特例去记，行情一变就失灵；抓住大趋势才耐用。","d01":"掷一枚硬币10次，出现8次正面。似然回答的是：「如果正面概率是 p,这批数据出现的可能性多大？」写作 L(p)=P(数据|p):固定看到的数据，变动 p 来比较。p=0.5 时，L=C(10,8)×0.5¹⁰≈0.044;p=0.8 时，L≈0.302——数据更「偏爱」p=0.8。关键区分：似然不是「p=0.8 的概率是30%」,它只比较假设，本身不是参数的概率。后验概率才回答：「看过这批数据后，p=0.8 的概率多大？」由贝叶斯公式 P(p|数据)∝L(p)×P(p) 得到——用数据支持度给先验信念加权。两者方向相反：似然是给定参数看数据，后验是给定数据看参数。条件变化：数据越多，似然曲线越尖锐；若硬币其实公平，数据支持 p=0.8 的程度会随次数增加而崩塌——似然驱动信念更新，但不单独等于信念。","d07":"冰淇淋销量越高，溺水人数越多——数据真实相关，但没人会说吃冰淇淋导致溺水。共同原因是夏天：天热既让人买冰淇淋，也让更多人下水。这类隐藏的「混杂变量」是相关不等于因果的最常见原因。判断依据：相关只说明两个量同涨同跌；因果还要求时间先后、作用机制，并排除其他解释。一个有力的检验是控制混杂：只在同样炎热的日子里比较冰淇淋与溺水，若相关消失，说明它原是混杂造成的；若仍存在，因果嫌疑才上升。迁移：常喝咖啡的人心脏病多？可能是吸烟者更爱喝咖啡，而吸烟伤心脏——按吸烟与否分层后相关若消失，因果就是假象。最干净的办法是随机实验：随机分组让混杂因素在各组间均匀分布，剩下的差异才主要归因于处理本身。","d02":"Variance answers: how spread out are the numbers? Take data 2, 4, 6. The mean is 4, so deviations are −2, 0, 2 — but deviations always sum to zero, so averaging them directly is useless. Squaring fixes that: 4, 0, 4, averaged gives variance σ² = 8/3 ≈ 2.67. Squaring does two jobs: it stops positive and negative deviations from canceling, and it weights big deviations heavily — one far-off point dominates the result. One wrinkle: units. If the data are meters, variance is in m²; taking the square root gives the standard deviation (≈1.63 m here), back in readable units. Change one condition: double every value (4, 8, 12) — deviations double, but squaring makes variance four times larger (10.67). So spread in plain units scales with the numbers, variance with their square. Use variance when big errors hurt disproportionately; use standard deviation to state spread simply.","d08":"Compound growth means gains start earning gains. At 10% a year, $100 becomes 110, then 121, then 133.10 — last year's interest itself earns interest: A = P(1+r)^t. This is why the starting amount matters more than intuition suggests. Growth is multiplicative: the ratio stays fixed, but the absolute gap widens. $200 vs $100 at 10% for 30 years ends at about $3,490 vs $1,745 — an initial $100 gap grew into $1,745. Starting earlier works the same way, since time sits in the exponent. Change one condition: cut the rate from 10% to 3.6%, and by the rule of 72 (doubling time ≈ 72/r years) doubling slows from about 7 years to 20. The same math drives population growth and viral spread, which is why small early differences become decisive — and why early contributions often beat later larger ones.","d06":"A cache keeps a fast local copy so the app doesn't refetch data on every request. Cache invalidation is what keeps that copy from lying: when the source of truth changes, stale copies must be removed or refreshed. Example: a product page is cached; the price drops in the database. Until the copy is invalidated, shoppers keep seeing the old price. Two common policies: a TTL — expire everything after, say, 60 seconds — simple, but every change is wrong for up to 60 s; or explicit invalidation — the price update also deletes the cached key, forcing the next read from the database. Change a condition: raise the TTL to an hour and pages render faster, but prices stay wrong longer; speed is paid for in staleness. The hard part at scale is that copies live in a CDN, an app cache, and browsers — one change must reach them all. App showing old data after you updated it? Suspect invalidation.","v04":"Idempotency means performing the same operation twice has the same effect as performing it once. Distributed systems need it because of retries. Networks are unreliable: a client sends a payment request, the timeout fires, yet the server may have already processed it. The client cannot tell, so it retries — and without idempotency the customer is charged twice. The fix: the client attaches an idempotency key (a unique request ID); the server records keys it has seen and returns the stored result for repeats — two requests, one charge. Some operations are naturally idempotent: GET, SET x=5, DELETE (deleting an already-deleted row is harmless). Others are not: ADD 10 to a balance applied twice adds 20. Change a condition: if a message queue offers at-least-once delivery, retries are guaranteed, so consumers must dedupe by message ID. The rule to carry over: any operation that can be retried should be safe to retry.","v02":"Search for 'jaguar' and the engine returns 20 links; 6 are relevant, and suppose 15 relevant pages exist. Two different questions, two scores. Precision: of what we retrieved, how much is right? 6/20 = 30%. Recall: of everything relevant, how much did we find? 6/15 = 40%. The example shows they pull apart. Return only the single safest link: precision may hit 100% while recall falls to 1/15. Return the whole index: recall is 100% while precision is tiny. Loosening or tightening what you return trades one for the other. Which matters more depends on the cost of each mistake: a spam filter needs precision — flagging a real email is costly; a cancer screen needs recall — missing a case is costly. Adding more results raises recall, usually lowering precision. F1 summarizes the balance, but choosing the balance is a decision about errors, not something a formula can decide for you.","d04":"You have a free afternoon. Options: study for Friday's exam, take a paid tutoring shift worth $50, or nap. Opportunity cost is the value of the single best option you give up. Choose studying, and your cost is not 'everything I could have done' — it is the $50 shift, since that beats napping. This is why free time never is: the afternoon gets spent either way, and the next-best alternative is the real price. Note what does not count: money you already paid last week for a canceled class is a sunk cost — gone regardless of today's choice — so it stays out of the comparison. Change one condition: the exam moves to next month. Studying's value today drops, the $50 shift becomes the better use, and the rational choice flips. Transfer this to any decision: compare each option against the best alternative, not against zero — that is how you see the true price of 'just staying home'.","v07":"路灯是典型的公共物品：不排他——无法只让付钱的人使用；不竞争——多一个人走在灯下，不减少别人的光。这造成搭便车：不出钱也照样享受，何必出？人人都这样想，路灯就没人建——人人受益的东西反而供给不足。关键机制是收益分散、成本集中：对单个家庭，独自出钱不划算，尽管大家一起建对所有人都划算；个体理性加总成集体非理性，这不是简单的自私，而是「无法排他」本身摧毁了收费的可能。条件变化：小区只有几十户、能互相监督收物业费，路灯就容易建——人数少、可监督，搭便车被抑制；收费电视能设密码排他，就从公共物品变成可收费的私人物品。迁移：开源软件、防洪堤面临同样困境；理解这一点，就明白这类东西为何常需要税收或组织来供给。"}
